note: Originals for the philosophy track (phil.1–7, gate-phil). Built by scripts/build_course_texts.py --only <ids> into course_data/texts/<id>.json. Plato is cited by Stephanus page (the Perseus editions divide by page only).

passages.title: Chaerephon asks the oracle
passages.author: Plato
passages.blurb: Chaerephon asks at Delphi whether anyone is wiser than Socrates; Socrates sets out to test the god's answer.

passages.title: Meeting at the King's Porch
passages.author: Plato
passages.blurb: Euthyphro finds Socrates at the King Archon's porch: someone has brought a public charge against him.

passages.title: Always in public
passages.author: Xenophon
passages.blurb: Where Socrates spent his days, and the questions he always asked: what is just, what is unjust?

passages.title: The slave boy and the square
passages.author: Plato
passages.blurb: Socrates questions Meno's slave about a square, to show that learning is recollection.

passages.title: The ring of Gyges
passages.author: Plato
passages.blurb: Glaucon's story of the shepherd who finds a ring of invisibility, and what a just man would do with it.

passages.title: The cup of hemlock
passages.author: Plato
passages.blurb: The poison is brought; Socrates prays, drinks it calmly, and scolds his weeping friends.

passages.title: The death of Socrates
passages.author: Plato
passages.blurb: Socrates' last words, a cock for Asclepius, and Phaedo's judgement of his friend.

passages.title: Xenophon's oracle
passages.author: Xenophon
passages.blurb: Xenophon's version of the Delphic answer: no one freer, juster or more self-controlled than Socrates.
